messages:
Alex: Heads-up — we've been seeing ingestion spikes from mobile routes. Question: should we do head sampling for interactive routes and tail sampling for background batch jobs? Need ideas on tiered sampling + retention so we don't lose debugability for customers.
Maria: +1 on mixed approach. interactive = head (keep first N spans per trace), batch = tail (keep last errors). saves volume.
Rahul: cost note — exporters bill by span count. Tail retains failures which are high value for alerts/QA. Head is cheaper but we miss late failures.
Olivia: what if we expose a per-tenant sampling policy in the Console so customers can opt-in to higher retention for specific routes? minimal UX: toggle + slider for p(keep) per route.
James: UX should default safe: permissive for enterprise tiers, aggressive for free/experimental. We need canary and an audit trail for changes. :thumbsup:
Alex: thinking about implementation: dynamic sampler that evaluates route + customer_tier + recent error rate. Pseudocode idea: \n```\nif tier == "enterprise": keep_all()\nelif route in interactive: head_sample(keep_first=3)\nelif route in batch: tail_sample(prob=0.02, keep_errors=True)\nelse: dynamic_prob = base_prob * error_multiplier(); sample(dynamic_prob)\n```\nMaria: Agree. Also add a cost-budget per-tenant so we auto-adjust sampling when a tenant blows quota. That avoids noisy tenants blowing our ingest.
Rahul: How do we signal sampling decisions in traces? If downstream tools need to know whether a trace was sampled we should add a span attribute like `sample.reason` and `sample.policy`. That also helps offline analysis.
Olivia: +1 for `sample.policy` tag. And in Console show the "sampling rule source" next to the trace (policy, override, budget).
SRE-bot: alert: telemetry-pipeline-ingest rate hit 85% of capacity in us-west last 10m — throttling may start at 90%.
Alex: ok that's urgent. Proposal: short-term emergency change: apply head sampling (keep_first=1) on non-enterprise mobile routes for next 30m, then revert. Can someone push the deploy?
Kyle: I can roll that. For safety I'll implement as a rollout flag `telemetry.sampling.emergency.mobile_head_v1` and do a 100% rollout to non-prod then 100% to prod if green.
Kyle: config snippet I'll use: \n```\nsampling_rules:\n  - id: mobile_non_enterprise_head_v1\n    match: "route:mobile & tier!=enterprise"\n    action: { type: "head", keep_first: 1 }\n    ttl: 1800 # seconds\n```\nJames: For longer term we should persist historical sampling directives and show them in the audit log (who toggled, why, delta in span volume). That helps SRE and billing.
Rahul: Also capture `exporter.truncated=true` when we drop spans due to budget so downstream billing + analytics isn't silently skewed.
Maria: question: how do we handle traces where head sampling removed an upstream span that later caused an error? We need a fallback to capture full trace if a downstream error is observed within X seconds.
Olivia: implement an "error-triggered backfill": if downstream span has status=error and parent was sampled_head, enqueue a background fetch to pull missing spans for that trace (best-effort). Could be async and rate-limited.
Alex: good. TODOs: 1) Kyle to push emergency head rule for mobile (30m TTL) 2) Rahul + Maria to spec `sample.*` span attrs and `exporter.truncated` flag 3) Olivia + James to mock Console UI for per-route policy + audit 4) SRE to watch ingest after change.
Kyle: starting rollout to prod canary now. ping when done.
SRE-bot: deploy-bot: rollout event recorded — telemetry.sampling.emergency.mobile_head_v1 -> canary -> 2025-09-10T15:12:03Z
Kyle: canary looks good, increasing to 100% in 5m. no errors so far.
Alex: thanks everyone. We'll debrief after ingest stabilizes and file a follow-up RFC for stale/backfill semantics and console controls. :white_check_mark:
